Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our demo/discovery and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Key takeaways
- Primary use case: low-latency inference for customer-facing chat and backend batch scoring (fraud scoring enrichment).
- Success criteria: sub-200ms 95th-percentile latency, 40% reduction in per-call unit cost vs current provider, and SOC2-aligned controls for audit logging.
- Current blockers: security questionnaire, procurement SOW review, and identification of the economic buyer for budget sign-off.

Proposed next steps
1) I’ll share the demo recording + a lightweight stakeholder map template (attached) for your internal use.
2) Could you introduce me to the procurement/legal contact who manages vendor questionnaires? You mentioned Tom in procurement — can you connect us?
3) Rishi (cc’d) will build a talk track / slide with ROI bullets tailored to your fraud use case so you have a concise one-pager to bring to the economic buyer.
4) If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min intro with procurement next week to walk through the security questionnaire and evidence items.

Attachments: Redwood-demo-recording-0303.mp4 (recording), Stakeholder-map-template.xlsx

Thanks — excited to keep momentum.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa —

Nice call notes. I put together a short talk-track outline and ROI bullets you can share with Alex/Priya and the economic buyer. Draft below — let me know if you want it converted into a 1-slide PDF.

Talk track (one-liner): Redwood reduces inference unit cost and stabilizes latency at scale so Finovate can deliver consistent end-user experience while cutting model-serving spend.

Top ROI bullets
- Expected token-cost reduction: 35–45% (batch + prefix caching for repeat queries)
- Operational uplift: fewer incidents from autoscaling gaps; typical reduction in time-to-recover for inference incidents by 60% vs unmanaged endpoints.
- Time to value: POC in 2–3 weeks with a limited dataset; Dedicated pools available for production readiness.

Procurement/security asks (short):
1) High-level SOC2 attachments we can provide (we have an SOC2 report + summary of logging controls).
2) Network diagram and data flow explanation for private deployment options (if they need an on-prem/VPC solution).
3) Standard SOW template and commercial term sheet for reserved capacity.

If you want, I’ll stitch this into a 1-pager that focuses on the economic buyer’s priorities (cost savings, runtime reliability, compliance).

-Rishi
